name: Australian Aborigines Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Bauer, Anastasia. 2014. The Use of Signing Space in a Shared Sign Language of Australia (Yolngu Sign Language). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton / Ishara Press.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Monograph on Yolngu Sign Language structure (note: YSL has its own Glottolog entry); could contain remarks on prosody of signs. Low expected yield for word stress.

sources.citation: Jorgensen, Eleanor, Jennifer Green & Anastasia Bauer. 2021. Exploring phonological aspects of Australian Indigenous sign languages. Languages 6(2): 81. doi:10.3390/languages6020081
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. The paper is a sign-language phonology (handshape inventories, handedness/symmetry/dominance, body locations, signing space) for Warlpiri, Kukatja and Yolngu sign; a full-text search for stress/prosod/accent/syllab/rhythm finds no statement about stress or prominence in the prosodic sense (the only 'prominence' hits refer to handshape frequency). Movement and non-manuals are named as parameters but not analysed.

sources.citation: Kendon, Adam. 1988. Sign Languages of Aboriginal Australia: Cultural, Semiotic and Communicative Perspectives. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press (reissued 2013).

sources.note: The only book-length structural description of Australian Indigenous sign languages (Warlpiri, Warumungu etc.); if anything has been said about movement prominence/rhythm in these sign languages it would be here. Low expected yield for a 'word stress' statement given the signed modality.
